Using an orchard-to-glass approach, founders Nick and Holly focus on heritage cider apples rarely found in modern cider production, creating ciders that showcase the character and complexity of the fruit itself. The cidery began in 2017 after the pair discovered an antique cider press and started making cider for friends and family. What began as a passion project quickly grew into one of the most awarded cideries in the Pacific Northwest. Since 2019, Puget Sound Cider Company has earned more than 80 awards at regional, national, and international competitions, including honors from the Northwest Cider Cup, Great Lakes International Cider & Perry Competition, Portland International Cider Cup, and CiderCraft Awards. We make dairy the long way, fermenting live cultures into fresh local milk, then churning it slow. Thick, tangy and alive with flavor. Every batch starts with intention. We’re not here to chase trends. We’re here to honour the craft we grew up with. To take something simple and do it properly. Hellenika is our way of keeping old techniques alive while making something new. Seasonal. Emotional. Tied to place. That place is here. Pike Place shapes everything we do. We steep MarketSpice tea into our mix when the grey sky rolls in. We use Sunny Honey when the bees are flying. We cook with neighbors at Atrium Kitchen because food should be shared, not just sold. The Greek cultures we use have been in our family for generations but, the flavors are born from this street, this city, this market. Nothing we make is static. That’s the beauty of cultured food. Fantello Farmstead Creamery began in 1918 in Enumclaw and continues to use the same farm-to-table methods. The Fantellos make cheese that is truly handmade every step of the way, from milking the cows into cans and hand dumping the milk into the vats, pail by pail, to aging in on wooden boards to make cheese as pure as possible. As a Hilltop Tacoma native, Juanita grew up seeing poverty first-hand and understands the importance of accessibility to fresh produce. When the family first started their urban farming journey, they found that they were selling many of their microgreens to chefs and the wealthy. Baby Chavs wants to change this perception and encourage healthy eating by making microgreens more approachable and versatile in every American household. Both their indoor and outdoor spaces are maximized to optimum efficiency. Their microgreens are practically soil free! Baby Chavs use mostly coco coir, the discarded fibers of coconuts, as a growing medium, along with a touch of soil to help with fertilizing. Coconut fibers contain nutrients optimal for plant growth. It can be easy to overlook other areas of the Seattle food scene. One of those areas that has been neglected far too long is Seattle donuts. That’s why in 2019, we decided to bring the Underground Donut Tour to Seattle and make sure that these amazing donuts got the attention they deserve. On the Underground Donut Tour, you’ll experience the 4 most unique donut shops Seattle has to offer. Starting in Belltown and working our way towards Pike Place Market, we’ll give you some history around each donut shop, the surrounding area, as well as highlights around Seattle history. You’ll be able to taste some of the most interesting flavors around created by professionally trained pastry chefs, as well as some of the freshest beignets you’ve ever had. We’ll finish the tour at Pike Place Market where you can see donuts made before your eyes at Daily Dozen Doughnuts . You’ll leave the tour full of Seattle history as well as tasty

They happily converted their land from a Christmas tree farm to a family farm that now includes beautiful flowers, herbs, veggies, and chickens. Phong and Ma’s son Chai is on the farm every day tending to the crops and maintaining the equipment. He says that he loves getting his hands dirty and having the freedom to run his own business with his family. Chai wasn’t always interested in farming, but after working for the Parks Department for several years, he noticed he was spending more and more of his free time on the farm and that farming was his true passion. Shong Chao’s produce is a mainstay of the PIKE BOX CSA , and often provides the program with unique vegetables like yu choy, garlic chives, and many varieties of leafy greens. Family members farm close by, so they can spend time together daily; they also share a greenhouse and cooler space. When living in Laos, Lee farmed rice and corn with his family and has continued his family’s farming tradition here in Puget Sound. Owner Dave Alberg carefully cultivates a 20 acres orchard in Royal City, Washington, about 170 miles southwest of Seattle. Never sprayed with chemicals and pruned to a minimum, the original cherry trees Alberg planted in the 70s still produce fruit to this day. Alberg Cherry is known for having some of the very first Washington state cherries of the season and attributes this head-start to the warm weather east of the Cascade mountains. Their table is packed with bundles of cherries, apricots, apples, and pears when the season kicks off in early June. Don’t hesitate to swing by – the growing window for cherries is short and sweet – often wrapping up by the end of July! _page.text: AG Family Farm - Pike Place Market Skip to content See Who's Open Parking & Directions Plan Your Visit About the Market Programs & Events Directory Market Map --> --> Your Market Day English Chinese (Simplified) English French German Hindi Russian Spanish --> show holiday graphics on home: false --> Home Directory AG Family Farm AG Family Farm About Us AG Family Farm proudly grows and distributes a variety of fresh, certified-organic fruit including peaches, apricots, nectarines, prunes, plums, cherries, pie cherries, and apples. Located in small-town Quincy, Washington, Arturo and his brother Roberto purchased 75 acres of land in 1998. They farmed together for several years under the name ACMA Mission Orchards. In 2013, the brothers sold a 10-acre parcel to their father who also farms organically, and they divided the remaining acreage into two separate parcels, each now farming independently. _page.text: Lid Wear - Pike Place Market Skip to content See Who's Open Parking & Directions Plan Your Visit About the Market Programs & Events Directory Market Map --> --> Your Market Day English Chinese (Simplified) English French German Hindi Russian Spanish --> show holiday graphics on home: false --> Home Directory Lid Wear Lid Wear Shop Now About Us Lid Wear owner Sarah Goldenberg, aka Goldie, handcrafts beautiful and practical hats for every walk of life and occasion. Goldie hitchhiked her way to Seattle from Washington, DC in 1978, landing in the Emerald City with just $10 worth of dimes in her pocket. She fell in love with the city and has been here ever since. Its primary public service activity is production of HistoryLink.org, the free online encyclopedia of Washington state history and the nation’s first original encyclopedia of community history created expressly for the Internet. Pike Place Market Tours HistoryLink’s tours explore the nine acres that comprise Pike Place Market with an eye on its architecture. As you wind through the Market’s organically grown labyrinths, note the “humble and anonymous” buildings and the human sense of scale that incubated a diverse and robust Market community. Although growth slowed by the 1930s, the Market’s importance as a gathering place remained paramount to Seattle’s citizens, and in the 1960s, when the Market was threatened with demolition, they created a “Keep the Market” campaign to save it. Thank goodness he did! He makes high-quality, one-of-a-kind objects out of mostly reclaimed and/or salvaged wood, both hardwood and softwood. His favorite wood to work with is the native to Washington State spalted bigleaf maple. Some Backstory In 2008, Todd thought he had found his calling in terms of a life career, working five years in cabinetry. Then, as the housing market bubble was rearing its ugly head, he was laid off at the beginning of 2009. In the meantime, Todd figured he should try to teach himself how to make more stuff out of wood other than boxes. So he began making all kinds of things to spruce up his house and make custom pieces for friends. He eventually moved back to his home state of Washington and has been experimenting and making one-of-a-kind objects even more with access to high-quality PNW wood. Todd has been at Pike Place Market since 2017 but only opened his woodworking business in November 2023. https://dogwooddork.sq

In the early 1900s, Lowell’s was a combination coffee roaster, peanut roaster, and cafeteria that served the citizens of Seattle when they visited the Market to purchase farm fresh produce, seafood, and dairy goods. The flagship store of Manning’s Cafeteria then became Lowell’s in 1957, and has remained so ever since. From the front entrance in the main arcade of Pike Place Market, it is unlikely that most visitors realize Lowell’s actually has three floors of seating—all offering world-class views of the Olympic Mountains, the ferries crossing Puget Sound, and a seagull’s view of the Port of Seattle. On the first and third floors, you order first with the cashier/barista and then find a view seat and your food will follow you shortly. While it is essentially a single exhibit wall, it occupies a sizable chunk outside Old Seattle Paperworks . The Museum displays part of the collection of Danny Eskenazi, who became obsessed with giant shoes after he’d learned that his grandfather had once owned a wingtip worn by Robert Wadlow, the world’s tallest man. Eskenazi offered $1,000 to anyone who could find that Wadlow shoe. It remains lost, but his efforts led to the discovery of the other shoes that are now displayed in the Museum. The Dressing Room is the standalone restaurant to the Can Can Culinary Cabaret, making it theatrically centered in its design. Just like Can Can’s Dinner Theatre , “The Dressing Room” features a menu of French-inspired Pacific Northwest fare, sourced fresh and direct from our neighbors in the historic Pike Place Market. All of The Dressing Room’s menu items rotate seasonally to coincide with each main stage show at the Can Can Theatre. Not all restaurants can say their menu selections are artfully inspired by the shows it produces. Dried flower wreaths are another specialty item we offer in addition to seasonal holiday wreaths and eucalyptus wreaths. The luminescence and fluidity of sea life is magical to her, and living in the Pacific Northwest has been the perfect backdrop to spark that creativity. As a young child, Tisbury lived on a boat in the Caribbean and was always connecting with the environment in some way or another. This has been a subject for Tisbury’s artwork for many years. Tisbury has been making glass art for over 25 years and began selling her creations at Pike Place in 2001. Each piece is hand-crafted using rods of glass melted with a torch flame to a temperature of over 2000 degrees. While the glass is molten hot, she uses different techniques to shape the glass. He then sanded each wooden box 8 times to the smoothest finish, hand rubbed with oil to a fine sheen and a fine display of the artistry of nature. The fine desk clocks are also treated with the same care. These boxes are created from woods from all over the world as well as the Northwest. Kris uses some woods that you can no longer acquire. He even has some of the original beams from when they first built Pike Place Market. Kris can also create a box from your own wood if you have a piece that is sentimental to you. vendors.name: Yarn Dragon
vendors.blurb: Formerly known as MJ Yarns, Yarn Dragon is the creative venture of Jonathan Berner. He began his knitting journey in 2008 with the intention of creating his own clothing to contribute to environmental sustainability.

vendors.name: Mobii
vendors.blurb: When Emmanuelle Shih opened her shop, Möbii, it soon became a popular destination for travelers who had seen her design on fellow adventurers.

vendors.name: No Boundaries Books
vendors.blurb: Deneen Shank of No Boundaries Books makes sustainable handmade leather journals fastened with elegant gemstones, clasps, snaps, or leather ties. These journals are ideal for writing, drawing, photography, scrapbooking and more!

vendors.name: Orna’s Pottery
vendors.blurb: Orna has been selling handmade pottery at Pike Place Market since 2005. Orna’s work is inspired by the rich natural environment of the Pacific Northwest and by indigenous pottery-making traditions from around the world.

vendors.name: Paper Scissors Rock
vendors.blurb: Paper Scissors Rock’s whimsical mandala stones are casted and handpainted by artist Pam Corwin. Pam says she never paints the same design twice, which means every stone is a one-of-a-kind piece of art.

vendors.name: Pattern & Posy
vendors.blurb: PATTERN & Posy is a brand of handmade, block-printed home and infant products by surface pattern designer and printmaker Carrie Narducci. Carrie’s product line includes tea towels, napkin sets, cork coasters, and organic infant onesies, hats, and bibs.

vendors.name: RamonaClaire
vendors.blurb: Ramona Golinveaux creates beautiful art and magnets using rolled-up recycled paper on canvas. She also pasts inspiring words on top.

vendors.name: Rock-n-Roll Woodwork
vendors.blurb: Ryan Sanderson of Rock-n-Roll Woodwork hand makes inlaid wall art featuring pop culture and nature themes. The goal of Rock-n-Roll Woodwork is to create beautiful yet badass, inlaid wall art.

vendors.name: Royal Phoenix
vendors.blurb: Phoenix Nalyvayko of Royal Phoenix is a fine art and fantasy photographer creating high-quality images that are meant to create a mood, inspire and uplift. Each photo is printed on canvas and then carefully hand-stretched by Phoenix.

vendors.name: Sabando Design
vendors.blurb: Ron and Kristeena Sabando of Sabando Design is a husband and wife silversmith team that hand-crafts each piece creating one-of-a-kind jewelry.

vendors.name: Rachel’s Raindrop® Jewelry
vendors.blurb: Rachel's Raindrop® Jewelry is hand-crafted by Silversmith Rachel Strodtbeck. Rachel creates unique modern silver and gold jewelry pieces that are made to fit comfortably and stand the test of time.

vendors.name: Seppa Designs
vendors.blurb: Ernie Seppa makes handcrafted sterling silver earrings and paper prints of original drawings, primarily of what he has seen in his nearly 50 years at Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Spearman Designs
vendors.blurb: Stephanie Spearman of Spearman Designs creates unique hand-crocheted, knitted hats and accessories. Stephanie is no stranger to the Market selling on our Daystall tables since 1981.

vendors.name: Tiny Fairy Houses
vendors.blurb: Are you looking for something whimsical and completely unique? Kristi Ringger's handmade ceramic fairy houses might exactly be what you're looking for.

vendors.name: Flyingcat Creations
vendors.blurb: Mutsuko Mitsui of Flyingcat Creations creates delightful and whimsical ceramic cups, mugs, earrings, necklaces, and cartoon-style drawings.

vendors.name: Frantic Art
vendors.blurb: Frantic Art is a husband and wife team that creates handmade ceramic light switch covers and functional pottery. They’ve been selling their pottery in the Pike Place Market since 1973.

vendors.name: Fusion in Glass
vendors.blurb: Fusion in Glass offers incredibly gorgeous, beautiful, and original fused dichroic and enameled glass pieces by Seattle glass artist Kyle Kinsey. His product line includes pendants, necklaces, rings, and earrings in all shapes, sizes, and colors.

vendors.name: Grey Day Candles
vendors.blurb: Grey Day Candles is a family business owned by Shane Gregory. Their signature candles are multi-layered with alternating scents on each layer, so your senses stay tantalized.

vendors.name: Seattle Hairwraps
vendors.blurb: Amy DeAguero has been selling her handmade products at Pike Place Market since 1988. Her unique and colorful hair wraps fit hair at least 2 inches long and works in fine baby hair or super curly strands. Also on her table, Flip Clips and Pony Tail Wraps.

vendors.name: I’m Just Kidding
vendors.blurb: The Munko Family of I'm Just Kidding, LLC is a two-generation business selling an assorted range of unique artwork and clever sayings on T-shirts, onesies, aprons, and tote bags.

vendors.name: Isis Ray
vendors.blurb: Isis Ray sells her vividly intricate handmade glass beads and jewelry under her name, Isis Ray. Isis has been melting glass to create flame-worked beads since 1985.

vendors.name: Jim Chow Jewelry
vendors.blurb: Jim Chow is a stone enthusiast who has been selling his handmade jewelry at Pike Place Market since 1975.

vendors.name: John Wiley Photography
vendors.blurb: John Wiley moved to Seattle from Alaska in 1985 with the hope of launching his photography business, John Wiley Photography.

vendors.name: Kate Endle Illustration & Fine Art
vendors.blurb: Kate Endle of Kate Endle Illustration & Fine Art uses a truly original style of multi-medium art to create collaged canvases, prints, home décor, paper products, and children's books. (She is the illustrator for the Caspar Babypants album covers.)

vendors.name: KiMonoMono
vendors.blurb: Linda Hoshide from KiMonoMono creates scarves, jewelry, and other accessories out of her collection of Japanese fabric. Linda’s work is clean, fun, modern, and traditional, and great for both formal or casual occasions. She is inspired by her heritage of being a Japanese American and her background in graphic design.

vendors.name: Kitten Mittens
vendors.blurb: Warm your paws and free your claws with fingerless mittens from Kitten Mittens by Jennifer Gay! These mittens are upcycled from repurposed wool and cashmere sweaters that are sure to keep your hands cozy and warm.

vendors.name: Delza
vendors.blurb: Formerly known as Knuckle Kiss. Our small batch and one-of-a-kind pieces are designed and handcrafted by Angela Delarmente in her Seattle studio.

vendors.name: KOBO Art Garden: Kaiju Glass Garage
vendors.blurb: KOBO Art Garden is a fine handmade glass art small business created by couple Joshua Swanson and Motoko Hayashi. They create one-of-a-kind pieces that are perfect for your home and garden.

vendors.name: KSWB Leather
vendors.blurb: Kasey Bracken of KSWB Leather creates handmade, laser engraved leather goods, specializing in journals that come in a variety of covers. KSWB only uses veggie tanned leather, which is not chemically treated and is healthier and better for you and the environment.

vendors.name: Leonarte
vendors.blurb: Leonardo Lanzolla of Leonarte is a self-taught contemporary artist from Torino, Italy. His paintings and prints are spontaneous, jovial, and intriguing reflecting the nature of mankind, modern life, and his senses.

vendors.name: 1976 It’s Just Art
vendors.blurb: Dan Gregory of It's Just Art has been honing in his funky and animated illustrations since he began drawing at the age of 5.

vendors.name: Aaron Murray Fine Folk Art
vendors.blurb: A ceramic artist for more than 25 years, Aaron Murray creates porcelain figurines and earthenware that combine his love of folk art and animal forms with a dash of humor.

vendors.name: Art By Harmony
vendors.blurb: Tlingit artist Harmony Hoss has sold her work at Pike Place Market since 2008.A Seattle native, Harmony is entirely self-taught, and her intricate prints are drawn freehand using pen and ink, acrylic paint, and colored pencils.

vendors.name: BasilicArt
vendors.blurb: Stacey Sterling of BasilicArt has been a working artist since 1980. Her mission is to bring people closer to the ocean and learn about environmental issues through murals, paintings, and clothing designs.

vendors.name: Buddha Bath
vendors.blurb: Bryan Roberts of Buddha Bath followed the motto of "return to basics" when developing his superior handcrafted bath and body care products. Buddha Bath's product line is designed to provide three benefits to your skin; cleanse, exfoliate & moisturize.

vendors.name: Careful It Bites
vendors.blurb: Kelice Penney of Careful It Bites is know for the wild, mystical, adorable and bizarre! Whether you need a mini yeti in specific colors, a one-of-a-kind toy for your nephew, or a full-size plush costume.

vendors.name: LTDesign
vendors.blurb: LTDesign has been making hand-dyed and screen-printed clothing and accessories at Pike Place Market since 2004.

vendors.name: Catshy Crafts
vendors.blurb: If you are looking for heartfelt wall art and small-batch felt goods, stop by Catshy Craft’s booth in Pike Place Market. Find cute dumpling hairclips, taco headbands, avocado badge reels and joyful felt flower bouquets that inspire warm and fuzzy feelings with every stitch.

vendors.name: Cloisonné Art
vendors.blurb: Cloisonné Art creates original handcrafted cloisonné jewelry that is colorful and whimsical. Cloisonné jewelry (from French: cloison = partition) is an enamel technique that uses wire to create unique shapes then filled with enamel.

vendors.name: CMS Ceramics
vendors.blurb: Chris Scamehorn of CMS Ceramics creates handmade and hand-painted ceramics inspired by the beauty of the Pacific Northwest. He is known for his “Stratascape Series” pottery, which he makes out of multiple colors of clay and hand-paints mountain landscapes on them.

vendors.name: Coastal Elevation
vendors.blurb: Angela Parriott's lifetime of curiosity grew into her business, Coastal Elevation, a combination of jewelry, accessories, clothing and textiles inspired by the organic beauty found in nature.

vendors.name: Crystal Bouquet
vendors.blurb: Crystal Bouquet creates beautiful night lights, pendants, plaques, and flowers arrangements by pressing and preserving locally grown flowers in beveled glass.

vendors.name: Cyclical Design Productions
vendors.blurb: Cyclical Design Productions by Ben Milam uses premium leather (recycled and new) to produce quality, handcrafted belts, bracelets, and guitar straps.

vendors.name: Do Not Bleach
vendors.blurb: In 2012, Noah Parriott of Do Not Bleach began selling uniquely designed t-shirts at Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: DrinkingStraws.Glass
vendors.blurb: DrinkingStraws.Glass is a husband and wife team that specializes in reusable glass drinking straws and carrying cases.

vendors.name: The Souk
vendors.blurb: The Souk owned by Songul Albayrak is a Middle-Eastern specialty food and gift shop near the First Starbucks along Pike Place.

vendors.name: Omart’s Lunch Counter
vendors.blurb: This three-generation, family-owned business operates an 18-seat lunch counter serving Filipino cuisine in the back of its Asian grocery store, which earned a prestigious 2020 James Beard Foundation "America's Classics" award.

vendors.name: Providence Heritage House at the Market
vendors.blurb: Heritage House is an assisted living facility that offers private apartments, nursing services, and a rich quality of life to seniors in the heart of our vibrant Marketplace. Staffed 24 hours a day, with nurses on site 16 hours a day, seven days a week. Heritage House brings together a wide range of services to meet resident’s needs.

vendors.name: The Market Commons
vendors.blurb: The Market Commons is a welcoming resource center that offers one-on-one support to navigate community resources and provides an array of community activities to bring neighbors together in Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Billie the Piggy Bank
vendors.blurb: Billie the Piggy Bank joined her cousin Rachel at the Market in 2011. She was the mascot for the Pike Place Market Foundation’s Pike Up! campaign, which raised more than $9 million to expand Pike Place Market, creating the MarketFront where Old Stove Brewing, Honest Biscuits, and indi chocolate are today.

vendors.name: Rachel the Piggy Bank
vendors.blurb: Rachel the Piggy Bank is the mascot of Pike Place Market and one of our best public fundraisers for The Market Foundation.

vendors.name: Virginia Inn
vendors.blurb: Located in Seattle’s Historic Pike Place Market, the Virginia Inn has been here serving Seattle fine food and drink since 1903.

vendors.name: Visit Seattle Information Booth
vendors.blurb: Need help locating a Market business? Or maybe you want some advice on where to start your Market Day. Stop by the Market Information Booth run by volunteers from Visit Seattle.

vendors.name: Wanderers’ Mail Service
vendors.blurb: Wanderers’ Mail Services was established in 1909 to help the men of the sea and prospectors wandering the gold fields have a safe and confidential place to receive their mail.

vendors.name: Emmett Watson’s Oyster Bar
vendors.blurb: Emmett Watson and Sam Bryant opened the city's first Oyster bar in 1979. It is cozy and casual spot with fresh oysters, fish and chips with plenty local beers on tap.

vendors.name: Wild Fish Poke
vendors.blurb: Wild Fish Poke has been serving healthy and delicious Hawaiian-Japanese-style poke bowls in Pike Place Market since December 2017.

vendors.name: Woodring Northwest
vendors.blurb: Since 1985, Woodring Northwest has made the finest specialty preserves, marmalades, chutneys, and pickles. This family-owned and operated company sells daily at Pike Place Market and runs their farm stand in Monroe, Wa, about an hour outside Seattle.

vendors.name: Studio Solstone
vendors.blurb: For 30 years, Michael and Sarah Yaeger have been producing "Watercolors Fresh Daily" at Studio Solstone.

vendors.name: Sunny Honey Company
vendors.blurb: Sunny Honey is a small family-owned company specializing in local, raw, unfiltered honey and beeswax goods. Started as part of the Pike Place Market Farm Program in 2010, Sunny Honey Co. is now a permanent part of the Market family with their little honey shop, open every day from 9-5!

vendors.name: Sunshine Jewelry
vendors.blurb: For 20 years, Sunshine Jewelry proudly provided beautiful jewelry to Seattle residents and visitors alike.

vendors.name: Sweetie’s Candy
vendors.blurb: Sweetie's Candy may be tiny but carries over 200 different products, including gums, liquid candy, gummy candy, hard candy, mints, PEZ, chocolate, nostalgic candies, and, of course, gifts for all your sweeties!

vendors.name: Taproom at Pike Place
vendors.blurb: Since 2018, the Taproom at Pike Place has been serving up a rotating selection of local craft beer, wine, and cider, alongside delicious food made from scratch daily.

vendors.name: Tenzing Momo
vendors.blurb: Tenzing Momo is the West Coast’s oldest herb store with more than 400 medicinal herbs and 100 fragrances and essential oils.

vendors.name: The Athenian Seafood Restaurant and Bar
vendors.blurb: Since 1909, the Athenian Seafood Restaurant and Bar has served delicious food and beverages in one of Seattle's most iconic restaurant settings.

vendors.name: The First Starbucks
vendors.blurb: The story of Starbucks begins in 1971 along the cobblestone streets of Seattle’s historic Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Three Girls Bakery
vendors.blurb: Selling savory croissants, delicious pastries, and freshly made bread -- Three Girls Bakery is a Pike Place Market staple in more ways than one.

vendors.name: Three Girls Bakery’s Lunch Counter
vendors.blurb: The Three Girls Bakery Lunch Counter serves a wide variety of soups and sandwiches made to order. Don't forget to try their Famous Meatloaf sandwich. They've been making Zelda's meatloaf recipe for over 30 years and it's a fan favorite.

vendors.name: Totem Smokehouse
vendors.blurb: Totem Smokehouse is a family-owned business that has been hand crafting wild smoked salmon for over 40 years in Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Truffle Queen
vendors.blurb: Whether you’re a Seattle visitor or a local, Truffle Queen is a must visit destination for wine lovers and foodies. They provide unique and delicious specialty foods and wines to customers online and in-store in Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Ugly Baby
vendors.blurb: Ugly Baby follows a mantra, "Unapologetic art for immature adults". We are Rosalie & Douglas Gale: inventors of Shower Art - waterproof art you can hang in your shower with a suction cup.

vendors.name: Umai Sushi & Teriyaki
vendors.blurb: Umai Sushi & Teriyaki focuses on various styles of takeout teriyaki and sushi.

vendors.name: Unexpected Productions Improv
vendors.blurb: For over four decades, Unexpected Productions has been the cornerstone of Seattle's improv scene, blending laughter, creativity, and community.

vendors.name: Urara
vendors.blurb: Urara is an authentic Japanese food restaurant dedicated to serve locals and tourists the highest quality foods and services at Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Ventures Marketplace
vendors.blurb: The Ventures Marketplace is an eclectic gift shop in the heart of Pike Place Market featuring jewelry, art, body care products, housewares, food pantry, and more.

vendors.name: Ruby’s Seattle Gift Gallery
vendors.blurb: Ruby's Seattle Gift Gallery offers customized jewelry and repairs. We specialize in diamonds and precious stones. Find Ruby's Seattle Gift Gallery on Level 5 of Pike Place Market’s DownUnder across from Sound View Café.

vendors.name: Saffron Spice
vendors.blurb: Saffron Spice seeks to take you on a culinary discovery of Indian food. If you are new to Indian food, try out the usual favorites like Chicken Tikka Masala and Chana Masala.

vendors.name: Seattle Cutlery
vendors.blurb: Seattle Cutlery began in 1978 as a dream to bring better knives to the city of Seattle. They offer high-end specialty knives for culinary use and the outdoors, plus sharpening.

vendors.name: Seattle Hats
vendors.blurb: Seattle Hats was established in Seattle in 1998 by local artist Jo Kaseter, whose line of hand-crocheted hats is perfect for newborns to adults.

vendors.name: Seattle Messenger Cooperative
vendors.blurb: Opened in 2015, Seattle Messenger Cooperative is a worker-owned and -operated messenger company servicing Seattle, the greater Western Washington area, and beyond.

vendors.name: Pizza & Pasta Bar
vendors.blurb: Recently remodeled, Pizza & Pasta Bar offers authentic Italian cuisine in Seattle’s iconic Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Sergio’s Barber Shop
vendors.blurb: Mix it up with a haircut at Seattle's Sergio's Barber Shop. Walk-ins are welcome at this shop in Post Alley. The barbers at Sergio’s Barber Shop will get you in and out in a flash, so head on over during your lunch break.

vendors.name: Shug’s Soda Fountain & Ice Cream
vendors.blurb: Shug’s Soda Fountain & Ice Cream is an independently owned family business specializing in ice cream, sundaes, homemade sodas, locally roasted organic coffee, and ice cream cocktails.

vendors.name: Shy Giant
vendors.blurb: Shy Giant, the first frozen yogurt business in Seattle, was opened in 1976.

vendors.name: Simply the Best
vendors.blurb: The story of Simply The Best began more than 30 years ago when Paul Sweat designed and built an alternative wood fueled dehydrator at his Omak orchard.

vendors.name: Sisters European Cafe
vendors.blurb: Sisters European Cafe specializes in European-inspired grilled sandwiches, soups and salads.

vendors.name: So Much Yarn
vendors.blurb: So Much Yarn is a local yarn shop offering beautiful yarns, expert instruction, and a friendly knitting and crochet community in the heart of downtown Seattle in Pike.

vendors.name: Solstice Designs by Locals
vendors.blurb: Solstice Designs by Locals is a bright shop located in Pike Place Market that promotes local artists and is the permanent home of Amy Harris’ beautiful handcrafted jewelry.

vendors.name: Sosio’s Produce
vendors.blurb: Sosio’s Fruit and Produce is the exclusive home of "Oh My God" Fruit. Peaches, pears, and melons that are oh so big and juicy get this exclusive label. You'll know it when you have tried a sample of these elite fruits.

vendors.name: Sound View Cafe
vendors.blurb: Sound View Café is a family eatery whose goal is to provide locally inspired dishes with fair prices coupled with a fantastic view of Puget Sound.

vendors.name: Storyville Coffee Company
vendors.blurb: Storyville Coffee Company at Pike Place Market is their first retail coffee shop featuring a full espresso menu, fresh baked and handmade Storyville pastries, Storyville Hardware products, and plenty of space for the customer to sit and enjoy the experience.

vendors.name: Pike Place Nutrition
vendors.blurb: Located on the 4th floor of the market, Pike Place Nutrition has been serving downtown Seattle with quality natural supplements since 1990.

vendors.name: Pike Place Nuts
vendors.blurb: Pike Place Nuts creates artisan nuts crafted in small batches following a Bavarian family recipe.

vendors.name: Pipe Palace
vendors.blurb: Established in 1969, Pipe Palace is the oldest, modern and traditional smoke shop in Downtown Seattle!

vendors.name: The Pink Door
vendors.blurb: The Pink Door is a restaurant-cabaret where fun and delicious Italian food makes for a memorable experience.

vendors.name: Piroshky Piroshky
vendors.blurb: Blending traditional recipes with PNW flavor, Piroshky Piroshky makes 32 different piroshkies daily, both savory and sweet.

vendors.name: Place Pigalle
vendors.blurb: Place Pigalle is a historic restaurant that pairs locally sourced French fare & Puget Sound views.

vendors.name: Polish Pottery Place
vendors.blurb: Polish Pottery Place sells authentic Polish pottery made from the most renowned ceramics maker in the region: Ceramika Artystyczna.

vendors.name: At Random Productions
vendors.blurb: At Random Productions is a Market stand offering t-shirts, tote bags, and aprons printed with zany graphics and Seattle cityscapes, as well as tie-dyed merchandise.

vendors.name: Neighborcare Health at Pike Place Market
vendors.blurb: Neighborcare Health at Pike Place Market provides a range of primary care health services for adults regardless of income or insurance.

vendors.name: Pure Food Fish
vendors.blurb: Pure Food Fish is a multi-generational fish market selling local fish and shellfish in Pike Place Market for more than 100 years.

vendors.name: The Cheese Box
vendors.blurb: Longtime Pike Place Market workers are now the new owners of The Cheese Box. An independent, standalone cheese shop in the Corner Market building.

vendors.name: Frank’s Quality Produce
vendors.blurb: Frank’s Quality Produce is a family owned and operated fruit and vegetable stand in Pike Place Market that specializes in locally sourced produce.

vendors.name: Rachel’s Ginger Beer
vendors.blurb: Rachel's Ginger Beer is made in Seattle using fresh lemons, strong roots, organic cane sugar, and top-quality water.

vendors.name: Radiator Whiskey
vendors.blurb: Voted one of the best new bars by Seattle Magazine in 2013, Radiator Whiskey opened as an instant classic.

vendors.name: The Raven’s Nest
vendors.blurb: The Raven’s Nest is a family-owned business focused on authenticity and curiosity. It was founded by Matthew Steinbrueck and now owned by his eldest son.

vendors.name: Rings-N-Things
vendors.blurb: Rings N Things has been selling nice and unusual gifts and jewelry for someone, or yourself, at reasonable prices since 1974.

vendors.name: Rotary Grocery
vendors.blurb: Rotary Grocery is a full-service convenience store and offers a full line of grocery items.

vendors.name: Pasta Casalinga
vendors.blurb: Pasta Casalinga serves up authentically artisanal pasta dishes in the heart of Pike Place Market. Owner Michela brings her Italian roots and Northwestern experiences together to produce rustic, homestyle cuisine to feed and create community.

vendors.name: Pike Market Food Bank
vendors.blurb: The Pike Market Food Bank provides free groceries to downtown Seattle residents experiencing food insecurity.

vendors.name: Market Street Bags
vendors.blurb: Market Street Bags is a luggage store in Pike Place Market selling suitcases, backpacks, shoulder bags, duffle bags, casual luggage, business cases, utility bags, travel accessories, and more.

vendors.name: Pike Place Bakery
vendors.blurb: Pike Place Bakery is a family-owned market stand selling donuts, bread, retail & custom cakes, and pastries to customers since 1983.

vendors.name: Pike Place Bar & Grill
vendors.blurb: Pike Place Bar & Grill is a great place to have some sea food and wine, try crab cake and enjoy a wonderful view of the market.

vendors.name: Pike Market Child Care & Preschool
vendors.blurb: Pike Market Child Care & Preschool serves families living and working in downtown Seattle by providing high-quality early learning and care for infants and children (through 5 years old).

vendors.name: Pike Place Chinese Cuisine
vendors.blurb: Pike Place Chinese Cuisine is a cozy informal eatery in Pike Place Market that offers a roster of Chinese standards in a no-frills setting.

vendors.name: Pike Place Chowder
vendors.blurb: Pike Place Chowder is Seattle’s iconic destination for award-winning chowder, nestled in the heart of Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Pike Place Dental
vendors.blurb: Pike Place Dental is committed to helping patients achieve the oral health they desire. Their goal is to provide exemplary dental care in a spirit of tender loving kindness.

vendors.name: Pike Place Fish Market
vendors.blurb: "We're the guys that throw the fish!" Located in Seattle’s Pike Place Market since 1930, Pike Place Fish Market has endured as the local favorite for fresh, wild, premium Pacific seafood.

vendors.name: Pike Place Flowers
vendors.blurb: Located at the gateway to the Market, Pike Place Flowers is a full-service florist on the corner of 1st Avenue and Pike Street.

vendors.name: Pike Place Gifts
vendors.blurb: For any of your Pike Place Market and Seattle-branded souvenir needs, visit Pike Place Gifts. Take home a gift for for your friends and family from their selection of collectible trinkets. Offerings include printed shot glasses, snow globes, mugs, t-shirts, and hoodies.

vendors.name: Pike Market Senior Center
vendors.blurb: The Pike Market Senior Center is accessible to anyone aged older than 55 and is open every day of the week, serving free breakfast and lunch.

vendors.name: The Miniature Car Dealer
vendors.blurb: The Miniature Car Dealer specializes in metal miniature replicas of classic or popular automobiles, airplanes and trucks.

vendors.name: Miss Cafe
vendors.blurb: Welcome to Miss Café! We offer a home-style, Turkish food experience in the heart of Seattle.

vendors.name: Moon Valley Organics
vendors.blurb: Moon Valley Organics is a sustainable skincare company created by Kim and Aaron Otto. Their product line started with just 4 bar soaps, a Rejuvenating Rub, Lip Balm, and of course the ever popular Lotion Bar. In 2005, Moon Valley introduced a line of medicinal salves with the help and guidance of Dr. Daniel Newman.

vendors.name: Northwest Tastings
vendors.blurb: Northwest Tastings is an artisanal food bar and tasting room located in Pike Place Market's DownUnder. Our wines are produced on our family-run vineyard near Quincy, Washington.

vendors.name: Old Seattle Paperworks
vendors.blurb: Old Seattle Paperworks specializes in unique, vintage posters and advertising art and is located next to the world-famous Giant Shoe Museum.

vendors.name: Old Stove Brewing
vendors.blurb: The vision for Old Stove Brewing Co. has always been to carry on Pike Place Market’s “Meet the Producer” tradition by producing amazing beer onsite.

vendors.name: Orange Dracula
vendors.blurb: Orange Dracula is a recreation of owner Chad Smith's favorite teenage shops. Imagine a Woolworth’s or an old Five and Dime, now imagine it run by the ADDAMS family. That’s the Orange Dracula!

vendors.name: Oriental Mart
vendors.blurb: Oriental Mart has been a mainstay of the Market since the 1970s. This three-generation, family-owned business offers a wide selection of traditional Asian spices, sauces and grocery products.

vendors.name: Osara Commissary
vendors.blurb: Osara Commissary features original artwork by Mikako Hamaguchi and offers a variety of cute and unique items from Japan.

vendors.name: Our Fabric Stash
vendors.blurb: Our Fabric Stash is an innovative, eco-friendly fabric consignment shop, designed for today’s Stash-aHOLic.

vendors.name: Pappardelle’s Pasta
vendors.blurb: A pasta stand located in the historic Pike Place Market in the heart of downtown Seattle.

vendors.name: Left Bank Books Collective
vendors.blurb: Left Bank Books has been a fixture of Seattle's radical community since 1973 when a group of people split off from the University District’s Red and Black Books to form their own collective bookstore in Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Pine Books
vendors.blurb: Step inside the newly remodeled Pine Books! Formerly Lion Heart Book Store, this bookstore in the Lower Levels of Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Los Agaves
vendors.blurb: Los Agaves was founded by Jaime Mendez and his family, and offers authentic Mexican cuisine and world-class Mexican and Mediterranean catering.

vendors.name: Lungu Gifts & Antiques
vendors.blurb: Welcome to Lungu Gifts, our boutique is inspired by the beautiful collection of authentic art, clothing and accessories.

vendors.name: Madame Lazonga’s Tattoo
vendors.blurb: Madame Vyvyn Lazonga, also known as “Seattle’s First Lady of Tattoo,” has been considered an icon in the realms of tattoo artistry since 1972.

vendors.name: Made in Washington
vendors.blurb: Made in Washington is a crucial destination for gifts which celebrate the best of Washington State: our food, our art, our lifestyle.

vendors.name: Maggie’s Shoes
vendors.blurb: Here at Maggie's Shoes, we offer an exceptional selection of men's and women's shoes that come straight from Europe.

vendors.name: Marakesh Leather
vendors.blurb: At Marakesh Leather we specialize in handmade leather belts and unique accessories for style and quality conscious men and women.

vendors.name: Mariscos Mexico
vendors.blurb: Taco lovers! Have you tried Mariscos México in the Economy Market? This little stand makes amazing seafood tacos like the Nut-Crusted Halibut, Acapulco Shrimp, Cod Fish Taco and the Mahi Mahi.

vendors.name: Market Coins
vendors.blurb: For over 50 years, this unique little shop has offered rare coins, political and sports memorabilia, plus a wide variety of reproduction posters at the famous Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Market Diner
vendors.blurb: Best burgers in the Market and home of the Seattle cheese steak made with Gorgonzola in a red wine demiglaze.

vendors.name: Market Grill
vendors.blurb: Market Grill has been serving up the best grilled fish in Pike Place Market since 1996.

vendors.name: Market Magic Shop
vendors.blurb: Located in Pike Place Market, the Market Magic Shop is the longest-running magic shop in the Pacific Northwest and 3rd oldest in the USA!

vendors.name: Market Optical
vendors.blurb: Eyewear isn’t just about vision. It’s also about style. Our superb opticians help you select the perfect frame for your face and your lifestyle.

vendors.name: MarketSpice
vendors.blurb: The history of MarketSpice can be traced back to a small tea and spice shop established in Seattle’s historic Pike Place Market in 1911.

vendors.name: Market Tobacco Patch
vendors.blurb: Market Tobacco Patch offers a wide variety of premium cigars, pipe accessories and vintage tins. The shop offers a well-organized humidor and a very knowledgeable owner who is excited to share his knowledge of tobacco.

vendors.name: MarninSaylor
vendors.blurb: MarninSaylor is Thomas Marnin and Skye Saylor, two country kids in the big city hand-making Donut Cats, Pastry Pets, and other toys.

vendors.name: Golden Age Collectables
vendors.blurb: Golden Age Collectables is the oldest comic shop in the world. Founded in 1961, they sell new and vintage comics, manga, collectibles, figurines, Funko toys, board games, movie scripts, vintage Star Wars toys, posters, and so much more.

vendors.name: Hands of the World
vendors.blurb: Hands of the World has an impressive 35-year history in Pike Place Market, matched only by the countries represented in the store—Nepal, Pakistan, Indonesia, Mali, Kenya, Thailand, India—to name a few.

vendors.name: Holy Cow Records
vendors.blurb: Holy Cow Records is a used record store in Seattle’s Pike Place Market. They specialize in rare vinyl LPs and 45s.

vendors.name: Honest Biscuits
vendors.blurb: Honest Biscuits was started by Art Stone, who learned biscuit making from his grandmother in rural North Carolina. Head to the Pike Place MarketFront off Western Avenue and grab one of their fried chicken Butterhole Biscuit Sandwiches.

vendors.name: House of Jade
vendors.blurb: House of Jade in Pike Place Market's DownUnder offers a wide selection of jewelry and precious stones. They also specialize in stone setting, casting, polishing, and repairs. This jewelry and souvenir shop has been calling the Market home since 1976. Find them near Sweetie's Candy and Lionheart Bookstore.

vendors.name: The House of Silver & Gold
vendors.blurb: Are you looking for some unique jewelry made up of gold or silver? Then stop by the House of Silver & Gold in the Lower Levels of Pike Place Market. This small shop offers a treasure trove of hidden gems.

vendors.name: IL Bistro
vendors.blurb: For nearly 50 years, IL Bistro has offered Seattle regional Italian cuisine in an intimate fine-dining setting.

vendors.name: indi chocolate
vendors.blurb: indi chocolate sources cacao beans directly from farmers and cooperatives to make small batch, single origin, dark chocolate.

vendors.name: Jack’s Fish and Chips
vendors.blurb: Owner Jack Mathers' 40 years in the fish business has given him plenty of experience on what makes pristine seafood, which you'll be sure to get at Jack's Fish and Chips.

vendors.name: Jack’s Fish Spot
vendors.blurb: At Jack’s Fish Spot, they pride themselves on serving Seattle’s freshest, finest fish at a fair price. Owner Jack Mathers is a Seattle native who has spent the last 40 years in the fish business.

vendors.name: Jasmine Thai Restaurant LLC
vendors.blurb: Welcome to Jasmine Thai Restaurant, your number one source of Thai food at Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Kubode
vendors.blurb: Kubode aims to provide a personalized browsing experience that perfectly mirrors in-store plant shopping.

vendors.name: Kitchen Basics
vendors.blurb: Welcome to Kitchen Basics, a Fiesta® dinnerware store! Kitchen Basics is a family-owned business and they are open seven days a week, all year-round. Kitchen Basics was established in 1984 in the historic Pike Place Market and continues to provide customers with high-quality & unique kitchen tools.

vendors.name: Lamplight Books
vendors.blurb: Lamplight Books features a curated selection of literature, philosophy, poetry, and children's books. They specialize in vintage, classic, and out-of-print books. Browse their shelves any day of the week in the Sanitary Market.

vendors.name: La Vaca
vendors.blurb: Hungry? Head to La Vaca. This tiny restaurant in Pike Place Market delivers tasty, inexpensive burritos, tacos, and tamales.

vendors.name: Le Panier
vendors.blurb: It began in 1983, when Le Panier opened its bakery doors onto Pike Place to bring a taste of France to Seattle for all to share.

vendors.name: Le Pichet
vendors.blurb: Le Pichet owners Jim Drohman and Joanne Herron opened Le Pichet in 2000 with the hope of recreating the personal, neighborhood-style restaurants they had come to love in France.

vendors.name: DeLaurenti Food & Wine
vendors.blurb: Since 1946, DeLaurenti Food & Wine has been Seattle’s most complete source of hard-to-find ingredients from around the world.

vendors.name: Don & Joe’s Pike Quality Meats
vendors.blurb: Don & Joe’s Meats began in 1969 with a commitment to offer the finest quality meats to their customers in a friendly and personalized manner.

vendors.name: Double Dorjee Tibet Shop
vendors.blurb: Double Dorjee is your one-stop shop to find unique Tibetan handicrafts. They also sell ritual items, fine jewelry, healing incense, prayer flags, and much more.

vendors.name: Earth Wind & Fire
vendors.blurb: Earth Wind & Fire Boutique is a unique women’s retail store offering specialty clothing, jewelry, and accessories

vendors.name: Ed Newbold Wildlife Artist
vendors.blurb: Ed Newbold is a Wildlife Artist who lives in Seattle, WA and has a store at the entrance of the Pike Place Market in downtown Seattle.

vendors.name: Eclipse Hat Shop
vendors.blurb: Love hats? Look no further than Eclipse Hat Shop. Owner Sharon Hagerty is an authorized Stetson hat seller. Find fedoras, custom fur felt and straw, millinery, and vintage hats.

vendors.name: El Borracho
vendors.blurb: El Borracho is one of the best places in Seattle to get your Mexican food fix and they're now serving 100% plant-based Mexican food.

vendors.name: El Mercado Latino
vendors.blurb: El Mercado Latino is a family-owned and operated Latin grocery located in Post Alley to the left of Choice Produce. Every time you walk into this shop, you'll discover something new, from their wall of hot sauce to unique spices from South America.

vendors.name: F & J Great Western Trading Co
vendors.blurb: F & J Great Western Trading Co. sells some unique, one-of-a-kind gifts from all over the world. You can get stuff for your desk, plaques for the wall, cups for your coffee, steins for your beer, or framed insects for... well, why not?

vendors.name: Falafel King
vendors.blurb: Yacob at Falafel King is one of the most kind and generous kings.

vendors.name: Farvahar Persian Cafe
vendors.blurb: Farvahar Persian Cafe specializes in authentic Persian cuisine. Their dishes include kebobs, lentil soup, hummus, sandwiches and salads. Pull up a seat to their counter or order takeout from this Persian lunch spot.

vendors.name: Folio: The Seattle Athenaeum
vendors.blurb: Folio is a non-profit member supported library and cultural center offering cultural and civic conversations, book and art discussions, intimate concerts, a circulating collection of donated books, and accessible work spaces with beautiful views at the heart of the historic Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Gradient Art Gallery
vendors.blurb: Gradient Art Gallery is a group of artists and friends who have opened the gallery to share their work with the world.

vendors.name: Gem Heaven
vendors.blurb: Gem Heaven offers a vast collection of high-quality minerals, crystals, fossils, and jewelry fit for any treasure hunter with an eye for sparkle and a curiosity to discover pieces forged thousands, or even millions of years ago.

vendors.name: Ghost Alley Espresso
vendors.blurb: Ghost Alley Espresso is one unique coffee shop with an equally unique history.

vendors.name: Glass Eye Studio
vendors.blurb: Founded in 1978 in Seattle’s famed Pike Place Market, Glass Eye Studio is one of the oldest and largest privately-owned hot shops in the country and served as a training ground for some of the most famed glass artists of the Pacific Northwest.

vendors.name: Chin Music Press
vendors.blurb: Chin Music Press is a curiously bibliophilic indie publisher located on the 3rd level of the DownUnder of Seattle’s historic Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Chocolate & Ice Cream Delight
vendors.blurb: Chocolate & Ice Cream delight offers a medley of sweet small bite treats ranging from truffles to scoops and blended drinks. Stop in to try one or more of over a dozen rotating flavors they keep in-house, or pick from their selection of specialty chocolates!

vendors.name: Choice Produce
vendors.blurb: Choice Produce sits on the corner of Post Alley and Pike Place, a family-owned business providing our city with a splash of color and an affordable alternative to the large impersonal supermarkets.

vendors.name: Christopher’s Lamp
vendors.blurb: Christopher’s Lamp is the formulation of the empathic clairvoyant and Spiritual Counselor, Darleen Christopher.

vendors.name: Chukar Cherries
vendors.blurb: In 1988, Chukar Cherries was launched on the family farm with one goal – to be your go-to source for extraordinary Pacific Northwest foods & gifts.

vendors.name: Cinnamon Works
vendors.blurb: Located in Pike Place Market, Cinnamon Works is one of the few scratch bakeries left in Seattle. Owner Michael Ruegamer opened the bakery’s doors over 37 years ago when he bought a small storefront and turned his baking hobby into a new career.

vendors.name: City Fish Co.
vendors.blurb: City Fish is one of the oldest seafood stands at the Market. Located in the heart of the main arcade, City Fish Co. is a must-see when at the Market.

vendors.name: Cobb’s Popcorn
vendors.blurb: Cobb’s Pike Place Popcorn is THE gourmet popcorn shop in Seattle. Some of their staple flavors include caramel, cheddar, and chocolate popcorn alongside many seasonal favorites. They also sell delicious mushroom and butterfly popcorn kernels.

vendors.name: Conscious Wear
vendors.blurb: Conscious Wear is an eco-friendly shop that focuses on clothing, accessories, and home décor made from hemp, wool, and khaki cotton.

vendors.name: Copacabana Restaurant
vendors.blurb: Don" Ramon and Hortensia Pelàez opened the doors of Copacabana in the Pike Place Market in June of 1964. Named for “Our Lady of Copacabana” shrine in La Paz, Bolivia, the restaurant stood as a symbol of hope and courage for the entire Pelàez family. The restaurant still remains family-owned and operated, where they continue the original informal and friendly atmosphere.

vendors.name: Crêpe de France
vendors.blurb: Crepe de France has been operating within Pike Place Market since 1991 as Seattle’s favorite restaurant creperié.

vendors.name: The Crumpet Shop
vendors.blurb: The Crumpet Shop is Seattle’s first and original crumpet baking company. Founded in 1976 by Gary Lasater, he called it The United Metropolitan Improved Crumpet Baking & Punctual Delivery Company. Customers just nodded and smiled and called it The Crumpet Shop.

vendors.name: Daily Dozen Doughnut Company
vendors.blurb: Daily Dozen Doughnut Company's famous mini-donuts have been crowd pleasers for years. You know they’re fresh when you can watch them come off the machine.

vendors.name: 3D Wood Puzzles
vendors.blurb: Are you looking for a unique gift? Since 2001, 3D Wood Puzzles has been selling one-of-a-kind, three-dimensional wood puzzles at Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: 6H Consulting
vendors.blurb: 6h Consulting is a marketing and brand strategy consultancy formed by Paul Neal. 6h has more than 25 years of experience collaborating with executives across a broad range of industries on the customer-facing aspects of business strategy.

vendors.name: Ageless Acupuncture
vendors.blurb: Our goal at Ageless Acupuncture is to help our patients, to extend Chinese medicine beyond our office, and to educate!

vendors.name: Alibi Room
vendors.blurb: The Alibi Room across from the world-famous Gum Wall in Post Alley is a cozy speakeasy-style restaurant serving up brick-oven pizza, salads and cocktails. It has long been a favorite bar for Northwest authors, writers, and artists alike.

vendors.name: Animal Gifts & Collectibles
vendors.blurb: Animal Gifts & Collectibles is a treasure trove of unique animal figurines. This shop is one of those unique places you will only find in Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Antique Touch
vendors.blurb: Antique Touch is a collector's dream, from antique teacups and saucers to salt & pepper shakers and figurines. Find Antique Touch on Level 3 of Pike Place Market.

vendors.name: Art Stall Gallery
vendors.blurb: The Art Stall is a cooperative women-run gallery selling original paintings and prints ranging from landscapes to portraits and animals.

vendors.name: Gallery ERGO
vendors.blurb: Gallery ERGO is an artist-owned gallery located in Seattle's historic Pike Place Market. They sell fine art originals, prints, apparel and puzzles.

vendors.name: Atrium Kitchen at Pike Place Market
vendors.blurb: The Atrium Kitchen provides tours of Pike Place Market with Cooking Classes and specializes in private events and corporate culinary team building. Owned and operated by Chef Traci Calderon, Atrium Kitchen is also home to Nourished Neighborhood, a non-profit community meal service.

vendors.name: BLMF Literary Saloon
vendors.blurb: BLMF Literary Saloon is proof that there are endless treasures to be found in the lower levels of Pike Place Market. For 26 years, J.B. Johnson has owned this cozy, lovingly curated store—ever since a guest at his book-filled home commented that he had “books like a motherf----er” (hence the name).

vendors.name: Bottega Gelato
vendors.blurb: Bottega Gelato opened in 2003 with one simple goal: to make the highest-quality gelato. Using Italian techniques, it is clear from the first bite that this is an authentic artisanal product.

vendors.name: Brooke Westlund Studio & Gallery
vendors.blurb: Brooke Westlund, a native Seattleite, has always loved art. She studied Photography, Art History, and Business at Western Washington University.

vendors.name: Can Can Culinary Cabaret
vendors.blurb: The Can Can Culinary Cabaret is an intimate 120 seat dinner theatre and production house. The venue's entertainment, food, and drink experience are unlike any other in the world.

vendors.name: Old Fashioned Candy Store
vendors.blurb: The Old Fashioned Candy Store offers one of the largest assortments of sweet treats in the Market. From recent additions to retro candies that date as far back as the 1950s.

vendors.name: Robot vs Sloth
vendors.blurb: Robot vs Sloth is a small shop dedicated to bringing Seattle the very best animal art and curated handmade animal-themed gifts for all ages. Owner La Ru (Lauren Rudeck) started her Pike Place Market story in 2012 when she partnered with a fellow Seattle artist to operate a small shop on Western Avenue called Ugly Baby and La Ru.

vendors.name: Pike Place Market Creamery
vendors.blurb: The Pike Place Market Creamery has been the Market's go-to spot for dairy, dairy alternatives, eggs and cow gifts since 1978.

vendors.name: Bonnie B’s Peppers & Hot Dogs
vendors.blurb: Bonnie B's Peppers pays homage to owner Dylan's mother. Using her recipes and bearing her name, they offers pickled peppers, sauces, pickled vegetables and pickles!
